references.text: The people also grumbled against Moses in the Desert of Sin because there was no food, and they expressed the same wish to have remained in Egypt.
At Kadesh the people again lacked water and accused Moses of bringing them out of Egypt to die in the wilderness.
The people spoke against God and Moses, complaining about the lack of water and food in the wilderness.
At the Red Sea the people accused Moses in a similar way and asked why he had brought them out of Egypt to die.
At Marah the people grumbled against Moses because of the bitter water.
The psalm describes how the Israelites grumbled in their tents and did not obey the voice of the Lord.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did in the wilderness.
Moses reminds the people how they provoked the Lord to anger at Massah, referring to this event.
It highlights the recurring pattern where the people interpret God's act of salvation as a deception aimed at their death.
It uses identical rhetoric about being brought out to die in a wretched place and links thirst to a lack of all food.
It illuminates the same theological crisis: the fear that life in the wilderness is a trap leading to death rather than life.
It reveals the same theological logic: the exodus was a deception intended to let them die in the wilderness instead of living in Egypt.
It creates a theological contrast: the people use the exodus as an accusation against God/Moses, while Moses uses it as a basis for prayer.
